description.narrative:
Project Goal: To contribute to better information of the public in Moldova on matters of public interest through improved media quality coverage, media skills and capacities.
Objective 1: To improve the professionalism of Moldovan journalists (men and women) and equip them with new skills by the end of the project (Journalism Training and Assistance)
Objective 2: To contribute to improving the key media laws and holding officials accountable for their implementation (Policy and Advocacy)
Objective 3: To build the financial, legal and organizational infrastructure for Moldovan School of Journalism - MSJ to become an independent legal entity (Organizational development)

sector.narrative: Media and free flow of information

description.narrative:
Under objective 1 following progress was observed (To improve the professionalism of Moldovan journalists (men and women) and equip them with new skills by the end of the project):
Moldovan School of Journalism (MSJ) continued its core mission to raise new generation of professional journalists by yearly courses, short trainings, discussion clubs, alumni events and meetings.
The most important adjustment from September 2023 onwards was shortening the long-term study programme from ten months to six months (September - March), for the first time, since the launch of the school.
Within the Press Clubs Annual Gala, 2023 edition, awards were provided to journalists and newsrooms to recognize their efforts in promoting quality journalism.
IJCs free legal aid service has continued to be a reliable tool for journalists facing various legal problems in their professional activities. They continued to receive requests from media workers.
Under objective 2 following progress was observed (To contribute to improving the key media laws and holding officials accountable for their implementation):
During 2023, the Parliamentary Joint Working Group (JWG), composed of media experts, including the IJCs Program Manager of the Media Policies, Legislation and Research Program, continued its efforts to improve the legal framework governing media activity.
IJC team actively monitored the implementation of the newly enacted Advertising Law and contributed to designing a guide for Broadcasting Council on administrative practices and public consultation will follow in 2024.
Under objective 3 following progress was observed (To build the financial, legal and organizational infrastructure for MSJ to become an independent legal entity):
MSJ conducted a marketing campaign and offered special promotions and discounts to attract new students, implemented targeted email marketing tactics to re-engage MSJs previous beneficiaries an introduce them to its new study programs.
Aiming at ensuring organizational development of MSJ, the school managed to adapt, develop and initiate 10 internal policies, such as: salary and human resources policy; monitoring and evaluation policy, financial and fundraising strategy, procurement policy, anti-corruption and gender policy, accounting policies and conflict of interest policy. All internal documents are in place and their usage is monitored internally.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
